target_review.reason: L138 expressly finds that the premises were given to DTTDC in 1985, necessarily after 9 June 1952. The frozen input independently contains the respondent’s pre-target assertion that the arrangement existed since 1985, so the timing target is substantively decided and input-supported.

The court said the arrangement was on rent and that DTTDC had exclusive possession, but its operative characterization remained “either sub-tenant or an assignee.” It did not separately determine all supplied subletting-route incidents, so NOT_DECIDED is the appropriate target rather than an affirmative C02 finding.

L142 does not separately find that the respondents divested themselves of all tenant rights; it leaves the characterization as “either sub-tenant or an assignee.” Treating the assignment route as NOT_DECIDED preserves that undifferentiated reasoning.

L142 substantively applies the possession question, finds the respondents failed to discharge the onus of showing retained legal control or possession, and consequently presumes DTTDC had exclusive possession. That is an operative satisfaction of the parting-with-possession route, while the frozen input lacks the cross-examination/agreement material on which the determination depended.

L138 records RW-1’s admission that the respondents never took any landlord permission before giving the premises to DTTDC, and L143 notes no prior permission in Ex.RW1/1 before holding section 14(1)(b) proved. A finding of no permission is sufficient to establish the narrower absence of written consent, but the decisive admission and agreement are absent from the frozen input.

The court stated the retained-legal-possession qualification in L131 and then rejected its application in L142 because the respondents did not carry the burden of showing retained legal control or possession and DTTDC was presumed to have exclusive possession. DEFEATED with fact_truth UNKNOWN correctly avoids converting the burden failure into a factual finding that retained possession was affirmatively false.
